claims.text: Compositionally engineered refractory high-entropy alloys can serve as improved low-activation structural materials for high-temperature plasma-facing components in fusion reactors.
Refractory high-entropy alloys are promising materials for high-temperature and nuclear applications.
Enriching a BCC refractory alloy in vanadium and chromium relative to tungsten and tantalum would lower its activation.
Tungsten is a current material choice for fusion plasma-facing or divertor applications.
Tungsten-based plasma-facing alloys have a high melting point and acceptable thermal conductivity.
Tungsten-based plasma-facing alloys suffer from brittleness.
Tungsten-based plasma-facing alloys exhibit problematic helium-bubble formation under irradiation.
Fusion plasma-facing materials experience high heat and particle fluxes, including helium exposure and neutron-induced radiation damage.
Representative plasma-facing testing should occur at temperatures of at least 1000 K with concurrent neutron and helium-ion irradiation.
High configurational entropy will produce a homogeneous, single-phase, preferably BCC microstructure in the proposed alloy.
A homogeneous single-phase HEA microstructure impedes irradiation-defect coalescence and maintains mechanical stability.
Selecting low-activation elements reduces the formation of long-lived radioactive isotopes.
High-entropy stabilization lowers atomic diffusion in the proposed refractory alloy.
Lower atomic diffusion diminishes radiation-induced defect aggregation and brittle-phase formation.
Reduced defect aggregation and brittle-phase formation improve toughness and structural integrity under fusion conditions.
The proposed refractory HEA will have high-temperature strength and ductility comparable or superior to tungsten-based systems.
The proposed refractory HEA will have significantly lower neutron activation and less irradiation-induced degradation than tungsten-based systems.
Formation of brittle intermetallic compounds could negate the alloy's benefits.
The optimal ratios of low-activation elements and long-term performance under continuous fusion conditions remain uncertain pending irradiation tests.
